stories.headline: KOSPI gives back 3% after Wednesday’s 6.6% jump as Samsung’s quarter falls short
stories.what: The KOSPI closed Wednesday at 6,012.44, up 6.63%, after SK hynix posted record quarterly revenue of ₩104.6 trillion and a 2026 shareholder-return plan worth more than ₩100 trillion. On Thursday it was down 3.0% by late morning after Samsung’s third-quarter results came in slightly below forecasts and its shares fell 6.6%; SK hynix edged up 0.4%.
stories.why: Korea is your largest exposure. Your dashboard still prices SCBKEQTG at its 26 Oct NAV, and the KOSPI is about 7% above that close even after today’s drop, so most of this week’s gain isn’t in your portfolio value yet. EWY, which you hold directly, rose 5.4% in New York on Wednesday.

related.label: Samsung’s results
related.headline: Record ₩107.4 trillion profit, slightly below forecasts; ₩30 trillion dividend approved
related.text: Revenue was ₩195.3 trillion. Bloomberg reports the chip division’s profit missed estimates, and a CLSA analyst told Bloomberg the shares fell on a lack of buybacks. The ₩4,601-a-share dividend is paid on 27 Nov.

stories.headline: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00%; two officials voted for a hike
stories.what: The FOMC voted 10–2 to leave its target range unchanged. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted a quarter-point increase. The statement described inflation as elevated and growth as strong. The Fed raised rates in September for the first time since 2023.
stories.why: Futures now price a strong chance of another hike at the 8–9 December meeting, and the 10-year Treasury yield closed just above 5%. Higher US rates tend to weigh on share valuations and support the dollar against the baht. A quarter of your portfolio is in US assets.

stories.headline: Alphabet misses on revenue and profit; its shares fall about 10% after hours
stories.when: Wed 28 Oct · after the US close
stories.what: Third-quarter revenue was $127.6 billion against $128.2 billion expected, and Search revenue of $63.4 billion also fell short. Cloud revenue doubled, but free cash flow turned negative at $9.1 billion as capital spending reached $51.4 billion. Analysts quoted by CNBC called it the first miss on both revenue and earnings in nearly four years.
stories.why: You don’t hold Alphabet directly. It is one of the largest companies in the S&P 500, which ES-US500RMF tracks through the iShares Core S&P 500 ETF. Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 1.5% and S&P 500 futures about 0.5% this morning.

stories.headline: Bank of Thailand holds at 1.00% and raises its growth forecast
stories.what: The Monetary Policy Committee kept the policy rate at 1.00%. It raised its 2026 growth forecast to 2.4% (2.1% for 2027), citing exports and investment tied to the AI cycle, and warned that inflation could overshoot its 2.1% forecast because of energy costs and the war in the Middle East.
stories.why: A hold was widely expected, so little changes for your Thai bond funds (3.7%) today. The bank also noted a weaker baht, driven by US policy expectations and oil prices.

stories.headline: Bitcoin slips back below $80,000 after the Fed decision
stories.what: Bitcoin traded just above $81,000 around the Fed decision and was near $79,800 this morning, down about 1.7% over 24 hours. Ether and BNB also fell.
stories.why: A modest move for the 6% of your portfolio held in crypto, most of it in Bitcoin.

briefly.headline: Brent stays above $110 on Iran tensions
briefly.text: CNBC reports Brent settled 1.3% higher at $115.32 on Wednesday, while Bloomberg reported prices dipping on signs of fresh diplomacy with Iran. The Bank of Thailand cited energy costs as an inflation risk.

briefly.headline: VN-Index edged up 0.27% to 1,766.65 on Wednesday
briefly.text: Banks led the gain while foreign investors stayed net sellers.

briefly.headline: Meta’s ~$95 billion AI-funding share sale moves ahead
briefly.text: CNBC reported on 26 Oct that Meta launched a stock offering of about $95 billion to fund AI expansion. Prospectus supplements were filed with the SEC on 26 and 28 Oct.

briefly.headline: Five of your smaller US stocks filed quarterly results
briefly.text: Teradyne, Fortinet, Universal Display, KLA and Enphase filed results with the SEC on 27–28 Oct. Together they are under 0.5% of your portfolio; the filings are linked here.
